text: Time to put Chapter 5 together. One scenario, both applications — Vulnerability Response and Security Incident Response working as two stages of the same security story.

A quarterly vulnerability scan flags a Critical-severity CVE on exactly two servers. One hosts an internal QA test environment. The other is a production database server behind the Patient Scheduling application — the same business-critical system this path's CMDB capstone modeled. Same CVE, same severity score, on paper, two identical findings.

The scan alone can't tell you which to fix first — it's a tie. But once Vulnerability Response correlates each hostname against the CMDB, the picture changes completely. The first CI supports only a QA test environment, no real users. The second CI, through CSDM's relationships, is the primary database server underneath the Patient Scheduling Business Service — something clinicians rely on every single day.

And that's the decision: fix the Patient Scheduling server first, ahead of the identical-severity QA finding, because only CMDB and CSDM correlation can see that one of these two supports something that actually matters and the other doesn't. The scanner alone was never going to make that call.

Then triage turns up something new: log evidence the vulnerability on that production server wasn't just present, it looks already exploited — an unexpected outbound connection, a login from nowhere familiar. That's the trigger. This stops being a Vulnerability Response problem alone. It's now a potential active compromise, and that means opening a Security Incident Response record.

The new record carries over the same CI and the same CVE context — exactly why these two applications live on one platform instead of two disconnected tools. It starts in Analysis, then moves straight to Containment: isolate the server, rotate any credentials it had access to, block the suspicious traffic — all before eradication even begins. Only once eradication and recovery are both genuinely complete does it move toward Review, feeding straight back into tighter remediation timelines for Business-Service-critical systems going forward.
Correlation drove the priority, evidence drove the escalation, and phase order kept the response honest. Chapter 6 picks up from here, starting with the elevated-privilege security_admin role.
